summary: The sitting senator ran again: Mark Warner (Democrat) won re-election over Bert Mizusawa (Republican).

candidates.name: Mark Warner
candidates.bio: Mark Warner has been a U.S. senator from Virginia since 2009 and was governor of Virginia from 2002 to 2006. Before politics he co-founded the venture capital firm Columbia Capital.

positions.summary: Supports abortion rights and Roe v. Wade.
Describes himself as an early champion of the Affordable Care Act and says he has worked to protect and strengthen it.
Voted for the 2025 Laken Riley Act.
Says he is focused on lowering costs for families and growing wages, and supports policies that help Americans adapt to AI and new technologies and encourage employer training.
Supports making education more affordable, student debt relief, industry certifications and lifelong learning.
Says he backs an "all-of-the-above" energy strategy that expands clean energy, boosts domestic production and modernizes the grid.

candidates.name: Bert Mizusawa
candidates.bio: Bert Mizusawa is a retired U.S. Army major general who describes himself as a four-time combat commander and a Silver Star recipient. He served as Deputy Under Secretary of the Army and as a Senate Armed Services Committee staff member, and holds degrees from West Point and Harvard. He won the 2026 Republican nomination for U.S. Senate in Virginia.

positions.summary: Says he will focus on balancing the budget, and promises to lower the tax on selling a home and reduce taxes on Virginia families.
Says he will lower costs by holding insurance companies accountable, fund rural hospitals and expand veterans' health care.
Has named border security as a priority.
Supports bringing new nuclear power online to reduce household energy costs, calling it "clean, cheap, reliable and safe."

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (political.org Nov 14 tally, AP called 34 of 35)
